program_name: Federal Scientific Research and Experimental Development Tax Incentive Program
funder: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Government of Canada
amount_notes: CCPC rate: 35% refundable ITC on first $3M qualified expenditures (federal proposals may increase limit to $6M pending legislation). 15% non-refundable ITC on excess. Other corporations: 15% non-refundable only. Labour: up to 69% of eligible salaries including overhead. Contractors: up to 36%. Materials: up to 45%.
organization_types_eligible: Partnerships and trusts conducting SR&ED in Canada
eligibility_criteria: Work must constitute scientific research or experimental development as defined in the Income Tax Act
Must address scientific or technological uncertainty through systematic investigation
Work must be carried out in Canada
Expenses must be incurred in connection with SR&ED carried on in Canada
Claim must be filed within 18 months of end of the tax year
exclusions: CRITICAL: Non-profit organizations and registered charities NOT eligible
Routine development without technological uncertainty does not qualify
Market research, quality control, and social science research excluded
Capital equipment expenditures made after January 1 2014 excluded from federal (but check provincial)
IRAP and other government assistance received reduces SR&ED expenditure pool dollar-for-dollar
Work performed outside Canada not eligible for ITC
notes: LARGEST federal R&D support program — $4.5B annually to 21,000+ claimants. NOT applicable to Emerge Academy Foundation (NFP). Emerge Academy Inc (for-profit OpsCo) may qualify IF it develops curriculum tech, athlete tracking systems, or other technology with genuine uncertainty. Sacral Solutions primary SR&ED candidate if health tech R&D exists. Stacks with Saskatchewan provincial SR&ED and NRC IRAP (IRAP reduces SR&ED pool). File via T661 and Schedule 31 with corporate tax return. 18-month absolute deadline — no extensions. August 2025 draft legislation marks most substantial program update in a decade — monitor for final legislation.
